output.text:
## Cover Letter, Executive Summary, and Company Overview

1. Cover Letter

[Date]

City of Marlow Vale
Planning Department
Procurement Office
[City Address]

Attention: Procurement Evaluation Panel

Re: Response to Request for Proposals RFP MV-2026-114 – Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System

Dear Members of the Evaluation Panel,

Tessellate Civic Software is pleased to submit this proposal in response to RFP MV-2026-114. We understand that the City of Marlow Vale requires a secure, accessible, and reliable platform to manage building permits from application through inspection to issuance, and we believe PermitFlow is well suited to that purpose.

PermitFlow is a purpose-built, software-as-a-service solution used by 41 local authorities to streamline permit workflows while maintaining rigorous security and audit standards. We are prepared to support the City of Marlow Vale's planning department, IT security officer, and procurement office through a transparent and straightforward implementation, drawing on our team's experience migrating data from systems similar to the one currently in use by the City.

This response addresses each of the twenty requirements in RFP MV-2026-114 individually and provides a compliance status for each. Where PermitFlow does not fully meet a requirement today, we state that clearly and describe the workaround, roadmap, or alternative we offer. We have done this because we understand that the City scores each requirement separately, and a complete and honest response is the most useful one for the evaluators.

We are available to provide demonstrations, references, or additional detail at any point in the evaluation process. Thank you for the opportunity to propose. We look forward to the possibility of working with the City of Marlow Vale.

Sincerely,

[Name]
Bid Manager
Tessellate Civic Software
[Email] | [Phone]


2. Executive Summary

Tessellate Civic Software proposes PermitFlow, a cloud-hosted, SaaS-only building-permit management platform, to replace the City of Marlow Vale's current system. PermitFlow is in active production at 41 local authorities and is designed to reduce manual effort, improve inspector throughput, and give applicants a clear, accessible view of their permit status.

PermitFlow is hosted in two data centres located within the same country as the City, 300 kilometres apart, with automatic failover. Measured availability over the trailing twelve months was 99.93%, and we offer a contractual monthly availability guarantee of 99.9% backed by service credits. All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Single sign-on via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect is available, multi-factor authentication is built in for all users and mandatory for administrators, and a full audit log of every view, change, and decision is retained for ten years and exportable as CSV. An independent penetration test is conducted annually, and the summary report is shared under NDA.

The public applicant portal meets WCAG 2.1 level AA and was independently audited last year. The internal staff screens meet most AA criteria; a recent audit identified fourteen open issues, which we commit to remediate within six months of contract signature. Online payment of permit fees is supported through integration with the City's existing payment provider. Inspectors use a native iOS and Android mobile app that works offline for viewing assignments, with results submitted when the device regains connectivity. Electronic plan review supports PDF and image markup in the browser; CAD (DWG) files must be converted to PDF before upload, as native DWG viewing is not supported.

PermitFlow includes a documented open REST API covering applications, inspections, and payments, thirty standard reports, and a drag-and-drop report builder with scheduled email delivery. Support is available 08:00–18:00 on working days by phone and email, with a 24/7 on-call line and a thirty-minute response target for severity-one incidents. Training is delivered through train-the-trainer sessions supplemented by online video materials.

Of the twenty requirements in RFP MV-2026-114, PermitFlow fully meets seventeen. Three requirements are partially met: custom roles (roadmap item, not yet available), fully offline mobile submission (results require connectivity), and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on internal staff screens (fourteen remediation items, six-month fix window). One requirement, on-premises deployment, is not met, as PermitFlow is a SaaS-only product. Each of these is addressed in detail in the Requirement Responses section, together with the workarounds or commitments we offer.

Tessellate Civic Software was founded in 2014 and employs eighty-five people, of whom a majority are dedicated to engineering, security, and customer success. We have migrated from the City's current product on two prior occasions, which positions us to minimise disruption during implementation. A detailed sixteen-week implementation plan is included in Section 6.

We are committed to an honest and complete evaluation. This response states our compliance exactly as the facts support, and we welcome any questions the panel may have.


3. Company Overview

Tessellate Civic Software is a civic-software company founded in 2014. We build and operate PermitFlow, a cloud-hosted building-permit management platform used today by 41 local authorities. The company employs eighty-five people, with the majority focused on platform engineering, information security, and customer success. All staff operate from the same country as the City of Marlow Vale, and all services are delivered from two data centres within that country, located three hundred kilometres apart with automatic failover between them.

Our product, PermitFlow, is a software-as-a-service solution. There is no on-premises version. The platform covers the full permit lifecycle: public application intake through an accessible portal, payment of fees via the authority's existing payment gateway, electronic plan review with in-browser markup of PDF and image files, assignment and execution of inspections via a native mobile app, and issuance of permits with full audit records. Reporting includes thirty pre-built reports and a drag-and-drop report builder with scheduled email delivery. A documented open REST API exposes applications, inspections, and payment data for integration with other municipal systems; workflow configuration is not exposed through the API.

Security is a central design principle. Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest with AES-256. Single sign-on is supported via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Multi-factor authentication is available to all users and is mandatory for administrative accounts. Access is governed by role-based controls with twelve predefined roles. Full audit logging captures every view, change, and decision, is retained for ten years, and can be exported as CSV. An independent penetration test is performed annually, and a summary report is provided to the customer under a non-disclosure agreement. Availability has been measured at 99.93% over the last twelve months, and the contractual guarantee is 99.9% per month with service credits.

Accessibility is likewise central. The public applicant portal meets WCAG 2.1 level AA and was independently audited in the past twelve months. The internal staff interface meets the majority of WCAG 2.1 AA criteria; the most recent audit identified fourteen open items, and we have committed to resolving them within six months of contract signature.

Support is provided from 08:00 to 18:00 on working days via phone and email. A 24/7 on-call line covers severity-one incidents—defined as a complete platform outage—with a thirty-minute response target. Onboarding includes train-the-trainer sessions and a library of online video materials to sustain staff competency over time.

Tessellate has prior experience migrating from the same product currently used by the City of Marlow Vale. We have completed two such migrations, performed by our own team from database exports, and we propose a similar approach for the City. We believe this direct experience, combined with the stability of a product already in production across 41 authorities, gives the City of Marlow Vale a low-risk path to a modern, secure, and accessible permit-management system.

## 4. Requirement Responses

## 4. Requirement Responses

### REQ-01 Cloud hosting within the country
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow is delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, hosted exclusively within the country in which the City of Marlow Vale is located. The platform is deployed across two independent data centres situated approximately 300 kilometers apart. This geographic distribution ensures data residency compliance while providing robust geographic redundancy. All permit data, including application details, uploaded documents, and user records, remains strictly within national borders. The hosting infrastructure is managed by Tessellate Civic Software, ensuring that all data handling practices comply with local data protection regulations and the city's requirement for domestic hosting.

### REQ-02 Availability of at least 99.9% per month
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software offers a contractual Service Level Agreement (SLA) guaranteeing 99.9% availability per month for the PermitFlow platform. This commitment includes a service credit mechanism for any period where availability falls below the guaranteed threshold, providing financial assurance to the City of Marlow Vale. Our operational track record supports this commitment; over the last 12 months, the measured availability of the PermitFlow platform across all customers was 99.93%, exceeding the required target. The architecture utilizes automatic failover between the two data centres mentioned in REQ-01, ensuring that minor infrastructure faults do not result in service interruptions. This high availability ensures that the city's planning department and applicants can access the system reliably during business hours and beyond.

### REQ-03 Single sign-on with the city's identity provider
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow supports enterprise-grade Single Sign-On (SSO) integration, allowing the City of Marlow Vale to leverage its existing identity infrastructure. The platform natively supports industry-standard protocols including SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. This allows city staff to log in to PermitFlow using their existing city credentials without needing separate usernames and passwords for the permit management system. By integrating with the city's Identity Provider (IdP), we centralize user authentication, simplify access management for IT administrators, and enhance security by enforcing the city's existing password policies and authentication standards directly through PermitFlow.

### REQ-04 Multi-factor authentication for all users
**Compliance: Full**

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a core security feature built into PermitFlow. It is mandatory for all administrator accounts to ensure the highest level of protection for system configuration and sensitive data access. For general users, MFA is fully supported and can be enforced according to the city's security policies. The system supports standard authentication methods, including Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) and other compatible factors. This layered security approach ensures that even if a user's password is compromised, unauthorized access to the permit system is prevented, significantly reducing the risk of data breaches for the City of Marlow Vale.

### REQ-05 Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow provides a robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system with 12 predefined roles that cover standard functions such as Administrator, Planning Officer, Inspector, Receptionist, and Public User. These roles grant or restrict access to specific features and data records within the system. However, the ability for the city to define completely new, custom roles is not available in the current production release; this functionality is on the product roadmap for implementation next year. 

*Workaround:* The current 12 predefined roles are designed to cover the majority of civic permit workflows. For most local authorities, these roles are sufficient to segregate duties effectively. If the City of Marlow Vale requires a unique role combination not covered by the predefined set, we recommend using the closest matching role and adjusting user assignments or utilizing the open API to manage specific record visibility if necessary. We can also discuss prioritizing the custom role feature based on the city's specific operational needs.

### REQ-06 Audit trail of all actions on an application
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow maintains a comprehensive and immutable audit log for every action taken within the system. This includes viewing an application, creating a new permit, modifying data fields, changing the status of a permit, uploading documents, and recording inspections or decisions. Each audit entry records the user who performed the action, the timestamp, and the specific nature of the change. This detailed history provides a complete chain of custody for all permit applications, supporting transparency, accountability, and dispute resolution. The audit trail is accessible to authorized city staff and is exportable, ensuring that the City of Marlow Vale can review and verify all historical activities on any application.

### REQ-07 Audit records retained for at least 7 years
**Compliance: Full**

The audit logs in PermitFlow are automatically retained for a period of 10 years. This retention period significantly exceeds the City of Marlow Vale's requirement of 7 years. The data is stored securely in the hosted environment and is readily available for retrieval. If the city requires audit data older than the standard retention period or needs a bulk export for archival purposes beyond the system's active search window, the audit logs are exportable in CSV format. This ensures long-term compliance with record-keeping regulations without requiring immediate manual archiving actions from city staff.

### REQ-08 Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
**Compliance: Full**

The public-facing applicant portal for PermitFlow meets the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards. This compliance was validated through an independent audit conducted last year. The portal is designed to be usable by applicants with a wide range of disabilities, including visual, auditory, physical, and cognitive impairments. Features include semantic HTML structure, appropriate color contrast, keyboard navigability, and screen reader compatibility. This ensures that all citizens of Marlow Vale have equal access to apply for and track building permits online, aligning with the city's commitment to inclusive digital services.

### REQ-09 All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
**Compliance: Partial**

While the public applicant portal is fully compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (as noted in REQ-08), the internal staff management screens currently meet most, but not all, AA criteria. An independent accessibility audit of the internal interface identified 14 open issues related to specific widgets and legacy forms. 

*Workaround & Commitment:* The internal screens remain functional for all staff, including those using assistive technologies for core tasks. However, to achieve full compliance, Tessellate Civic Software has committed to remediating all 14 identified issues within 6 months of contract signature. These fixes will involve updating UI components to ensure proper focus management, labeling, and keyboard support. We prioritize this remediation to ensure that all users, both public and internal, have equitable access to the system.

### REQ-10 Online payment of permit fees
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow integrates directly with the City of Marlow Vale's existing payment provider. This standard integration allows applicants to pay permit fees securely online at the point of application or when prompted during the review process. The payment gateway handles the transaction securely, and confirmation of payment is instantly recorded in the permit application record. This integration streamlines the revenue collection process for the city, reduces administrative overhead associated with manual payment processing, and improves the applicant experience by allowing immediate submission and payment in a single workflow.

### REQ-11 Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow includes a robust electronic plan review module that allows reviewers to mark up, comment on, and annotate PDF and image-based documents directly within the web browser. This tool supports standard redlining features such as drawing clouds, stamps, and text annotations. 

*Workaround:* The system does not support native viewing or markup of CAD (DWG) files. To review CAD drawings, the City of Marlow Vale requires applicants to convert DWG files to PDF before submission. We recommend enforcing this requirement in your submission guidelines. Once converted to PDF, the drawings can be fully reviewed and marked up within PermitFlow. This approach is widely used by other local authorities to maintain consistency in review files and ensure accessibility for all reviewers, regardless of their CAD software licensing.

### REQ-12 Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results
**Compliance: Partial**

The PermitFlow mobile app is available on both iOS and Android and is designed for use by inspectors in the field. The app supports offline viewing of assigned inspections, including access to permit details, approved plans, and previous inspection notes. 

*Workaround:* The app does not currently support offline submission of inspection results. Inspectors must wait until the mobile device reconnects to a network (via cellular data or Wi-Fi) to submit inspection outcomes, photos, and comments. We recommend that inspectors conduct their fieldwork and draft notes locally (if using a note-taking app outside the system) or ensure they are in a coverage area before attempting to submit results. If consistent connectivity is an issue in specific zones, inspectors should prioritize inspections in those areas last or return to a connected zone before closing out the visit.

### REQ-13 Encryption of data in transit and at rest
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow employs industry-leading encryption standards to protect the confidentiality and integrity of the City of Marlow Vale's data. All data transmitted between the user's browser/mobile app and our servers is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. Data stored within our hosted environment is encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption. These measures ensure that even if physical media were compromised, the data would remain unreadable. This dual-layer encryption strategy protects sensitive applicant information, proprietary plan details, and internal city correspondence from unauthorized access.

### REQ-14 Annual independent security testing
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software conducts an annual independent penetration test of the PermitFlow platform and its underlying infrastructure. These tests are performed by a reputable third-party security firm. The findings are used to identify and remediate potential vulnerabilities, ensuring the platform remains resilient against emerging security threats. A summary report of these security assessments is available and can be shared with the City of Marlow Vale under a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) to provide transparency into our security posture and validation of our controls.

### REQ-15 Documented API for integration
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow provides a well-documented, open REST API that facilitates integration with other city systems. The API currently covers core objects including Applications, Inspections, and Payments. This allows for automated reporting, data synchronization with asset management systems, or customer service tools. 

*Workaround:* There is currently no API endpoint available for configuring or modifying internal workflows (e.g., changing the approval steps for a permit type). Workflow configuration must be done via the administrative user interface within the application. For most integration scenarios involving data retrieval or status updates, the existing API is sufficient. If deep programmatic control over workflow logic is required, we can explore how to achieve specific outcomes using the existing API and UI combination.

### REQ-16 Migration of existing permit records
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software offers comprehensive data migration services as part of the implementation process. Our team has previously migrated data from the City of Marlow Vale's current permit system on two separate occasions, giving us specific familiarity with the data structures and potential challenges involved. The migration process involves extracting data from database exports of the legacy system, cleansing and transforming it to fit the PermitFlow schema, and loading it into the new environment. We manage this entire process, ensuring that historical permit records, applicant details, and associated documents are accurately transferred to PermitFlow, allowing for seamless continuity of service and historical reference.

### REQ-17 Standard and custom reporting
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow includes a powerful reporting engine designed to meet the analytical needs of the Planning Department. Out of the box, the system provides 30 standard reports covering key metrics such as permit volumes, approval rates, inspection status, and fee collection. Additionally, the system features a user-friendly, drag-and-drop report builder that allows city staff to create custom reports without technical assistance. These reports can be scheduled and automatically emailed to stakeholders at defined intervals, ensuring that the city maintains up-to-date visibility into its permit operations.

### REQ-18 Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software provides technical support to the City of Marlow Vale during standard business hours (08:00–18:00 on working days) via phone and email. For critical incidents defined as severity-1 (complete outage of the platform), we offer a 24/7 on-call support line. This dedicated line ensures that any total service disruption is addressed immediately, regardless of the time of day. We target a 30-minute response time for these severity-1 incidents, ensuring that the city's critical services are restored with minimal delay. Non-critical issues are handled within the standard business hours support framework.

### REQ-19 On-premises deployment option
**Compliance: Not met**

PermitFlow is provided exclusively as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. There is no on-premises version of the software available for deployment within the City of Marlow Vale's own data center. 

*Explanation:* Our business model is focused on cloud delivery to ensure that all customers benefit from the latest security patches, feature updates, and high-availability infrastructure without the burden of managing servers. The cloud hosting model described in REQ-01 ensures data residency within the country, mitigating many of the concerns often associated with off-shore cloud solutions. If the city has a strict requirement for on-premises hosting, PermitFlow may not be a viable option. However, for authorities seeking a modern, low-maintenance, and secure solution, the SaaS model offers significant advantages in total cost of ownership and agility.

### REQ-20 Training for staff
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software includes comprehensive training services in the implementation plan. We deliver train-the-trainer sessions designed to empower the city's internal leads to become proficient in PermitFlow and subsequently train other staff members. Additionally, we provide a library of online video tutorials covering all major user roles and functions, including administrator configuration, planner workflows, inspector app usage, and public portal guidance. This blended approach ensures that the City of Marlow Vale staff receives initial deep-dive training while having ongoing access to self-paced learning resources to support new hires or refresh skills.

## 5. Compliance Matrix

### Compliance Matrix

| Requirement | Status | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| REQ-01 Cloud hosting within the country | Full | Hosted in two data centres in the same country, 300 km apart, with automatic failover. |
| REQ-02 Availability of at least 99.9% per month | Full | Contractual SLA of 99.9%; measured availability 99.93% over last 12 months. |
| REQ-03 Single sign-on with the city's identity provider | Full | Supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect for SSO integration. |
| REQ-04 Multi-factor authentication for all users | Full | MFA built-in for all users; mandatory for administrators. |
| REQ-05 Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles | Partial | 12 predefined roles available; custom roles are on the roadmap for next year, not available today. |
| REQ-06 Audit trail of all actions on an application | Full | Full audit log of every view, change, and decision; exportable as CSV. |
| REQ-07 Audit records retained for at least 7 years | Full | Audit logs retained for 10 years, exceeding the 7-year requirement. |
| REQ-08 Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Full | Public portal meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA, independently audited last year. |
| REQ-09 All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Partial | Staff screens meet most AA criteria; 14 open issues to be fixed within 6 months of contract signature. |
| REQ-10 Online payment of permit fees | Full | Online payment via integration with the city's existing payment provider. |
| REQ-11 Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings | Partial | Supports PDF/image markup; no native DWG viewing (CAD files must be converted to PDF first). |
| REQ-12 Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results | Partial | Offline viewing supported; results can only be submitted when online (no offline submission). |
| REQ-13 Encryption of data in transit and at rest | Full | Data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). |
| REQ-14 Annual independent security testing | Full | Independent penetration test every year; summary report shared under NDA. |
| REQ-15 Documented API for integration | Partial | REST API covers applications, inspections, and payments; no API for configuring workflows. |
| REQ-16 Migration of existing permit records | Full | Migration performed by Tessellate team; prior experience with city's current system. |
| REQ-17 Standard and custom reporting | Full | 30 standard reports and drag-and-drop report builder; scheduled email reports. |
| REQ-18 Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents | Full | 08:00–18:00 support; 24/7 on-call for severity-1 incidents with 30-min response target. |
| REQ-19 On-premises deployment option | Not met | Hosting is software-as-a-service only; no on-premises version available. |
| REQ-20 Training for staff | Full | Includes train-the-trainer sessions plus online video tutorials. |

## 6. Implementation Plan

## 6. Implementation Plan

Our implementation plan is designed to deliver PermitFlow to the City of Marlow Vale within a strict 16-week timeline. As PermitFlow is a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform, our approach focuses on configuration, integration, data migration, and user adoption, rather than hardware installation or software deployment on local servers. We have successfully implemented PermitFlow for 41 other local authorities, and our methodology is standardized yet flexible enough to accommodate the City’s specific workflows.

The project is divided into five distinct phases. Below is the detailed breakdown of each phase, including the specific responsibilities of the City and Tessellate.

### Phase 1: Project Initiation and Setup (Weeks 1–2)

**Objective:** Establish the project foundation, define governance, and configure the core SaaS environment.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Project Kick-off:** Conduct a joint kick-off meeting with the City’s Project Manager, IT Security Officer, and Planning Department leads to finalize the project charter, communication plan, and escalation procedures.
*   **Environment Provisioning:** Provision the PermitFlow tenant in our secure, in-country data centers. This includes setting up the primary and failover environments.
*   **Core Configuration:** Configure basic system settings, including time zones, languages, currency (EUR), and email notification templates.
*   **Role Definition:** Set up the 12 predefined roles within the system and map them to the City’s existing job titles (e.g., Planning Officer, Inspector, Admin).

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Project Team Designation:** Appoint a dedicated Project Manager and a Technical Lead from the IT department to serve as primary points of contact.
*   **Stakeholder Identification:** Identify key users from the Planning Department who will provide input on workflows and testing.
*   **Infrastructure Access:** Provide necessary access details for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration, including SAML 2.0 metadata or OpenID Connect configuration files from the City’s Identity Provider (IdP).
*   **Approval of Configuration:** Review and approve the initial system configuration and role mappings.

### Phase 2: Data Migration and Integration (Weeks 3–7)

**Objective:** Securely migrate existing permit records and integrate PermitFlow with the City’s payment provider and identity provider.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Data Mapping:** Analyze the data structure of the City’s current permit system. We will create a detailed data mapping document correlating fields from the legacy system to PermitFlow.
*   **Migration Script Development:** Develop and test data transformation scripts. Having migrated from this specific product twice before, we will leverage existing knowledge of its schema to expedite this process.
*   **Payment Integration:** Configure the standard integration with the City’s existing online payment provider to enable fee payments via the public portal.
*   **SSO Configuration:** Finalize and test the SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect integration with the City’s Identity Provider to ensure seamless login and role-based access.
*   **First Data Migration Cycle:** Execute the first full data migration into the staging environment.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Data Extraction:** Provide database exports of all existing permit applications, inspections, payments, and user accounts from the current system in agreed-upon formats (e.g., SQL dumps, CSVs).
*   **Data Cleansing:** Review and clean data where possible (e.g., merging duplicate user accounts, correcting invalid addresses) before the final migration.
*   **Payment Provider Coordination:** Facilitate introductions or provide API keys/credentials required for the payment gateway integration.
*   **SSO Testing:** Collaborate with the IT Security Officer to test SSO login flows for various user roles and verify that multi-factor authentication (MFA) triggers correctly for administrators.
*   **Migration Validation:** Verify the accuracy of the migrated data in the staging environment against source records.

### Phase 3: Workflow Configuration and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) (Weeks 8–12)

**Objective:** Configure specific permit workflows, train super-users, and conduct rigorous testing.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Workflow Configuration:** Configure the permit application, review, and inspection workflows based on the City’s current and desired processes. This includes setting up routing rules for reviewers and inspectors.
*   **Report Configuration:** Set up the 30 standard reports and configure any custom reports required by the Planning Department using the drag-and-drop report builder.
*   **Super-User Training:** Conduct "Train-the-Trainer" sessions for designated super-users from the Planning Department. These sessions will cover administrative functions, workflow management, and report generation.
*   **UAT Support:** Provide a dedicated support channel for the UAT team to log issues and receive rapid feedback.
*   **Issue Resolution:** Address any defects or configuration issues identified during UAT.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **UAT Team Formation:** Assemble a UAT team comprising representatives from Planning, IT, and Finance.
*   **Scenario Testing:** Execute test scripts for end-to-end processes, including:
    *   Submitting a new application via the public portal.
    *   Assigning reviews and inspections.
    *   Processing payments.
    *   Viewing and marking up PDF plans in the electronic review tool.
    *   Submitting inspection results via the mobile app (online).
*   **Feedback and Sign-off:** Document test results, approve or reject configurations, and provide formal sign-off on the configured system once UAT is complete.
*   **Content Creation:** Draft and finalize standard email notifications, help texts, and public-facing instructions for the applicant portal.

### Phase 4: End-User Training and Final Data Migration (Weeks 13–14)

**Objective:** Train all end-users and perform the final data migration for production readiness.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **End-User Training Materials:** Provide online video tutorials and quick-reference guides for all user roles (Planning Officers, Inspectors, Admins). These resources will be available within the PermitFlow help portal.
*   **Final Data Migration:** Execute the final data migration into the production environment. This will be a "delta" migration to capture any changes made in the legacy system during the UAT phase.
*   **Data Verification:** Perform automated and manual checks to ensure data integrity in the production environment.
*   **Security Final Checks:** Confirm that all security settings, including MFA enforcement and audit logging, are active and configured as agreed.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Schedule Training:** Coordinate with Tessellate to schedule and announce the online training sessions to all staff.
*   **Staff Participation:** Ensure all users attend their designated training sessions and review the provided video materials.
*   **Legacy System Freeze:** Coordinate with the IT department to minimize or freeze changes to the legacy permit system during the final data migration window to ensure data consistency.
*   **Production Readiness Review:** Conduct a final review of the production environment with Tessellate to confirm readiness for go-live.

### Phase 5: Go-Live and Hypercare (Weeks 15–16)

**Objective:** Transition to live operations and provide intensive support during the initial weeks.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Go-Live Execution:** Switch the public portal and staff login URLs to point to the production environment. Disable access to the legacy system if agreed.
*   **Hypercare Support:** Provide enhanced support during the first two weeks of live operation. This includes daily check-ins with the City’s Project Manager and prioritized resolution of any live issues.
*   **Audit Log Verification:** Confirm that audit logs are capturing all activities as required for the first week of operations.
*   **Performance Monitoring:** Monitor system availability and performance metrics to ensure the 99.9% SLA is being met.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Public Communication:** Notify the public, developers, and other stakeholders that the new permit system is live and provide instructions on how to access it.
*   **Internal Communication:** Remind staff of the new login procedures and support channels.
*   **Legacy System Decommissioning:** Initiate the decommissioning process for the old permit system, ensuring all historical data is archived as required by the City’s retention policy.
*   **Issue Logging:** Report any live issues to Tessellate’s support team via the agreed channels.

### Post-Go-Live Support

After the 16-week implementation period, the City will transition to standard support services as defined in the RFP response. This includes business-hours support for general inquiries and 24/7 coverage for critical incidents (complete outage). The 14 open accessibility issues on internal staff screens identified in the pre-sales audit will be scheduled for remediation within the first six months post-contract signature, with regular progress updates provided to the City’s IT Security Officer.

This phased approach ensures a structured, collaborative, and low-risk transition to PermitFlow, leveraging our previous experience with the City’s legacy data to minimize migration risks and ensure a successful launch.

## 7. Pricing

7. Pricing

Tessellate offers a transparent and predictable pricing model for the PermitFlow platform. As a Software-as-a-Service provider, our pricing consists of an annual subscription fee that covers the core platform, infrastructure, and ongoing support, alongside one-off professional services fees for the initial implementation, data migration, and user training.

The following table outlines the costs associated with the City of Marlow Vale’s request for proposals (MV-2026-114). All prices are quoted in Euros (EUR) and are exclusive of VAT. No discounts are applied.

| **Cost Item** | **Type** | **Amount** | **Description** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Recurring | **€96,000** | Covers annual hosting, support services, and platform updates. |
| **Implementation & Data Migration** | One-off | **€38,000** | Covers system configuration, integration setup, and migration of existing permit records. |
| **Training** | One-off | **€6,500** | Covers train-the-trainer sessions and online video resources for staff. |

### Total Cost of Ownership

**First-Year Total**
The total investment required for the first year of service is **€140,500**. This figure includes the first annual subscription (€96,000), the one-off implementation and data migration fees (€38,000), and the one-off training costs (€6,500).

**Five-Year Total Cost**
Over a five-year period, the total cost is **€524,500**. This is calculated as five years of annual subscriptions (5 × €96,000 = €480,000) plus the one-off implementation, migration, and training costs (€38,000 + €6,500 = €44,500). 

This pricing structure ensures that the City of Marlow Vale receives a fully managed, high-availability solution with predictable ongoing costs. The annual subscription model eliminates the need for the City to invest in additional hardware or software licensing for the platform, allowing the Planning Department to focus its resources on community development and permit processing rather than IT maintenance.

1. Cover Letter

[Date]

City of Marlow Vale
Planning Department
Procurement Office
[City Address]

Attention: Procurement Evaluation Panel

Re: Response to Request for Proposals RFP MV-2026-114 – Cloud-Hosted Building-Permit Management System

Dear Members of the Evaluation Panel,

Tessellate Civic Software is pleased to submit this proposal in response to RFP MV-2026-114. We understand that the City of Marlow Vale requires a secure, accessible, and reliable platform to manage building permits from application through inspection to issuance, and we believe PermitFlow is well suited to that purpose.

PermitFlow is a purpose-built, software-as-a-service solution used by 41 local authorities to streamline permit workflows while maintaining rigorous security and audit standards. We are prepared to support the City of Marlow Vale's planning department, IT security officer, and procurement office through a transparent and straightforward implementation, drawing on our team's experience migrating data from systems similar to the one currently in use by the City.

This response addresses each of the twenty requirements in RFP MV-2026-114 individually and provides a compliance status for each. Where PermitFlow does not fully meet a requirement today, we state that clearly and describe the workaround, roadmap, or alternative we offer. We have done this because we understand that the City scores each requirement separately, and a complete and honest response is the most useful one for the evaluators.

We are available to provide demonstrations, references, or additional detail at any point in the evaluation process. Thank you for the opportunity to propose. We look forward to the possibility of working with the City of Marlow Vale.

Sincerely,

[Name]
Bid Manager
Tessellate Civic Software
[Email] | [Phone]


2. Executive Summary

Tessellate Civic Software proposes PermitFlow, a cloud-hosted, SaaS-only building-permit management platform, to replace the City of Marlow Vale's current system. PermitFlow is in active production at 41 local authorities and is designed to reduce manual effort, improve inspector throughput, and give applicants a clear, accessible view of their permit status.

PermitFlow is hosted in two data centres located within the same country as the City, 300 kilometres apart, with automatic failover. Measured availability over the trailing twelve months was 99.93%, and we offer a contractual monthly availability guarantee of 99.9% backed by service credits. All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Single sign-on via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect is available, multi-factor authentication is built in for all users and mandatory for administrators, and a full audit log of every view, change, and decision is retained for ten years and exportable as CSV. An independent penetration test is conducted annually, and the summary report is shared under NDA.

The public applicant portal meets WCAG 2.1 level AA and was independently audited last year. The internal staff screens meet most AA criteria; a recent audit identified fourteen open issues, which we commit to remediate within six months of contract signature. Online payment of permit fees is supported through integration with the City's existing payment provider. Inspectors use a native iOS and Android mobile app that works offline for viewing assignments, with results submitted when the device regains connectivity. Electronic plan review supports PDF and image markup in the browser; CAD (DWG) files must be converted to PDF before upload, as native DWG viewing is not supported.

PermitFlow includes a documented open REST API covering applications, inspections, and payments, thirty standard reports, and a drag-and-drop report builder with scheduled email delivery. Support is available 08:00–18:00 on working days by phone and email, with a 24/7 on-call line and a thirty-minute response target for severity-one incidents. Training is delivered through train-the-trainer sessions supplemented by online video materials.

Of the twenty requirements in RFP MV-2026-114, PermitFlow fully meets seventeen. Three requirements are partially met: custom roles (roadmap item, not yet available), fully offline mobile submission (results require connectivity), and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on internal staff screens (fourteen remediation items, six-month fix window). One requirement, on-premises deployment, is not met, as PermitFlow is a SaaS-only product. Each of these is addressed in detail in the Requirement Responses section, together with the workarounds or commitments we offer.

Tessellate Civic Software was founded in 2014 and employs eighty-five people, of whom a majority are dedicated to engineering, security, and customer success. We have migrated from the City's current product on two prior occasions, which positions us to minimise disruption during implementation. A detailed sixteen-week implementation plan is included in Section 6.

We are committed to an honest and complete evaluation. This response states our compliance exactly as the facts support, and we welcome any questions the panel may have.


3. Company Overview

Tessellate Civic Software is a civic-software company founded in 2014. We build and operate PermitFlow, a cloud-hosted building-permit management platform used today by 41 local authorities. The company employs eighty-five people, with the majority focused on platform engineering, information security, and customer success. All staff operate from the same country as the City of Marlow Vale, and all services are delivered from two data centres within that country, located three hundred kilometres apart with automatic failover between them.

Our product, PermitFlow, is a software-as-a-service solution. There is no on-premises version. The platform covers the full permit lifecycle: public application intake through an accessible portal, payment of fees via the authority's existing payment gateway, electronic plan review with in-browser markup of PDF and image files, assignment and execution of inspections via a native mobile app, and issuance of permits with full audit records. Reporting includes thirty pre-built reports and a drag-and-drop report builder with scheduled email delivery. A documented open REST API exposes applications, inspections, and payment data for integration with other municipal systems; workflow configuration is not exposed through the API.

Security is a central design principle. Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest with AES-256. Single sign-on is supported via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Multi-factor authentication is available to all users and is mandatory for administrative accounts. Access is governed by role-based controls with twelve predefined roles. Full audit logging captures every view, change, and decision, is retained for ten years, and can be exported as CSV. An independent penetration test is performed annually, and a summary report is provided to the customer under a non-disclosure agreement. Availability has been measured at 99.93% over the last twelve months, and the contractual guarantee is 99.9% per month with service credits.

Accessibility is likewise central. The public applicant portal meets WCAG 2.1 level AA and was independently audited in the past twelve months. The internal staff interface meets the majority of WCAG 2.1 AA criteria; the most recent audit identified fourteen open items, and we have committed to resolving them within six months of contract signature.

Support is provided from 08:00 to 18:00 on working days via phone and email. A 24/7 on-call line covers severity-one incidents—defined as a complete platform outage—with a thirty-minute response target. Onboarding includes train-the-trainer sessions and a library of online video materials to sustain staff competency over time.

Tessellate has prior experience migrating from the same product currently used by the City of Marlow Vale. We have completed two such migrations, performed by our own team from database exports, and we propose a similar approach for the City. We believe this direct experience, combined with the stability of a product already in production across 41 authorities, gives the City of Marlow Vale a low-risk path to a modern, secure, and accessible permit-management system.

parts.title: 4. Requirement Responses
parts.body:
## 4. Requirement Responses

### REQ-01 Cloud hosting within the country
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow is delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, hosted exclusively within the country in which the City of Marlow Vale is located. The platform is deployed across two independent data centres situated approximately 300 kilometers apart. This geographic distribution ensures data residency compliance while providing robust geographic redundancy. All permit data, including application details, uploaded documents, and user records, remains strictly within national borders. The hosting infrastructure is managed by Tessellate Civic Software, ensuring that all data handling practices comply with local data protection regulations and the city's requirement for domestic hosting.

### REQ-02 Availability of at least 99.9% per month
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software offers a contractual Service Level Agreement (SLA) guaranteeing 99.9% availability per month for the PermitFlow platform. This commitment includes a service credit mechanism for any period where availability falls below the guaranteed threshold, providing financial assurance to the City of Marlow Vale. Our operational track record supports this commitment; over the last 12 months, the measured availability of the PermitFlow platform across all customers was 99.93%, exceeding the required target. The architecture utilizes automatic failover between the two data centres mentioned in REQ-01, ensuring that minor infrastructure faults do not result in service interruptions. This high availability ensures that the city's planning department and applicants can access the system reliably during business hours and beyond.

### REQ-03 Single sign-on with the city's identity provider
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow supports enterprise-grade Single Sign-On (SSO) integration, allowing the City of Marlow Vale to leverage its existing identity infrastructure. The platform natively supports industry-standard protocols including SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. This allows city staff to log in to PermitFlow using their existing city credentials without needing separate usernames and passwords for the permit management system. By integrating with the city's Identity Provider (IdP), we centralize user authentication, simplify access management for IT administrators, and enhance security by enforcing the city's existing password policies and authentication standards directly through PermitFlow.

### REQ-04 Multi-factor authentication for all users
**Compliance: Full**

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a core security feature built into PermitFlow. It is mandatory for all administrator accounts to ensure the highest level of protection for system configuration and sensitive data access. For general users, MFA is fully supported and can be enforced according to the city's security policies. The system supports standard authentication methods, including Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) and other compatible factors. This layered security approach ensures that even if a user's password is compromised, unauthorized access to the permit system is prevented, significantly reducing the risk of data breaches for the City of Marlow Vale.

### REQ-05 Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow provides a robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system with 12 predefined roles that cover standard functions such as Administrator, Planning Officer, Inspector, Receptionist, and Public User. These roles grant or restrict access to specific features and data records within the system. However, the ability for the city to define completely new, custom roles is not available in the current production release; this functionality is on the product roadmap for implementation next year. 

*Workaround:* The current 12 predefined roles are designed to cover the majority of civic permit workflows. For most local authorities, these roles are sufficient to segregate duties effectively. If the City of Marlow Vale requires a unique role combination not covered by the predefined set, we recommend using the closest matching role and adjusting user assignments or utilizing the open API to manage specific record visibility if necessary. We can also discuss prioritizing the custom role feature based on the city's specific operational needs.

### REQ-06 Audit trail of all actions on an application
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow maintains a comprehensive and immutable audit log for every action taken within the system. This includes viewing an application, creating a new permit, modifying data fields, changing the status of a permit, uploading documents, and recording inspections or decisions. Each audit entry records the user who performed the action, the timestamp, and the specific nature of the change. This detailed history provides a complete chain of custody for all permit applications, supporting transparency, accountability, and dispute resolution. The audit trail is accessible to authorized city staff and is exportable, ensuring that the City of Marlow Vale can review and verify all historical activities on any application.

### REQ-07 Audit records retained for at least 7 years
**Compliance: Full**

The audit logs in PermitFlow are automatically retained for a period of 10 years. This retention period significantly exceeds the City of Marlow Vale's requirement of 7 years. The data is stored securely in the hosted environment and is readily available for retrieval. If the city requires audit data older than the standard retention period or needs a bulk export for archival purposes beyond the system's active search window, the audit logs are exportable in CSV format. This ensures long-term compliance with record-keeping regulations without requiring immediate manual archiving actions from city staff.

### REQ-08 Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
**Compliance: Full**

The public-facing applicant portal for PermitFlow meets the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards. This compliance was validated through an independent audit conducted last year. The portal is designed to be usable by applicants with a wide range of disabilities, including visual, auditory, physical, and cognitive impairments. Features include semantic HTML structure, appropriate color contrast, keyboard navigability, and screen reader compatibility. This ensures that all citizens of Marlow Vale have equal access to apply for and track building permits online, aligning with the city's commitment to inclusive digital services.

### REQ-09 All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA
**Compliance: Partial**

While the public applicant portal is fully compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA (as noted in REQ-08), the internal staff management screens currently meet most, but not all, AA criteria. An independent accessibility audit of the internal interface identified 14 open issues related to specific widgets and legacy forms. 

*Workaround & Commitment:* The internal screens remain functional for all staff, including those using assistive technologies for core tasks. However, to achieve full compliance, Tessellate Civic Software has committed to remediating all 14 identified issues within 6 months of contract signature. These fixes will involve updating UI components to ensure proper focus management, labeling, and keyboard support. We prioritize this remediation to ensure that all users, both public and internal, have equitable access to the system.

### REQ-10 Online payment of permit fees
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow integrates directly with the City of Marlow Vale's existing payment provider. This standard integration allows applicants to pay permit fees securely online at the point of application or when prompted during the review process. The payment gateway handles the transaction securely, and confirmation of payment is instantly recorded in the permit application record. This integration streamlines the revenue collection process for the city, reduces administrative overhead associated with manual payment processing, and improves the applicant experience by allowing immediate submission and payment in a single workflow.

### REQ-11 Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow includes a robust electronic plan review module that allows reviewers to mark up, comment on, and annotate PDF and image-based documents directly within the web browser. This tool supports standard redlining features such as drawing clouds, stamps, and text annotations. 

*Workaround:* The system does not support native viewing or markup of CAD (DWG) files. To review CAD drawings, the City of Marlow Vale requires applicants to convert DWG files to PDF before submission. We recommend enforcing this requirement in your submission guidelines. Once converted to PDF, the drawings can be fully reviewed and marked up within PermitFlow. This approach is widely used by other local authorities to maintain consistency in review files and ensure accessibility for all reviewers, regardless of their CAD software licensing.

### REQ-12 Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results
**Compliance: Partial**

The PermitFlow mobile app is available on both iOS and Android and is designed for use by inspectors in the field. The app supports offline viewing of assigned inspections, including access to permit details, approved plans, and previous inspection notes. 

*Workaround:* The app does not currently support offline submission of inspection results. Inspectors must wait until the mobile device reconnects to a network (via cellular data or Wi-Fi) to submit inspection outcomes, photos, and comments. We recommend that inspectors conduct their fieldwork and draft notes locally (if using a note-taking app outside the system) or ensure they are in a coverage area before attempting to submit results. If consistent connectivity is an issue in specific zones, inspectors should prioritize inspections in those areas last or return to a connected zone before closing out the visit.

### REQ-13 Encryption of data in transit and at rest
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow employs industry-leading encryption standards to protect the confidentiality and integrity of the City of Marlow Vale's data. All data transmitted between the user's browser/mobile app and our servers is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. Data stored within our hosted environment is encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption. These measures ensure that even if physical media were compromised, the data would remain unreadable. This dual-layer encryption strategy protects sensitive applicant information, proprietary plan details, and internal city correspondence from unauthorized access.

### REQ-14 Annual independent security testing
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software conducts an annual independent penetration test of the PermitFlow platform and its underlying infrastructure. These tests are performed by a reputable third-party security firm. The findings are used to identify and remediate potential vulnerabilities, ensuring the platform remains resilient against emerging security threats. A summary report of these security assessments is available and can be shared with the City of Marlow Vale under a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) to provide transparency into our security posture and validation of our controls.

### REQ-15 Documented API for integration
**Compliance: Partial**

PermitFlow provides a well-documented, open REST API that facilitates integration with other city systems. The API currently covers core objects including Applications, Inspections, and Payments. This allows for automated reporting, data synchronization with asset management systems, or customer service tools. 

*Workaround:* There is currently no API endpoint available for configuring or modifying internal workflows (e.g., changing the approval steps for a permit type). Workflow configuration must be done via the administrative user interface within the application. For most integration scenarios involving data retrieval or status updates, the existing API is sufficient. If deep programmatic control over workflow logic is required, we can explore how to achieve specific outcomes using the existing API and UI combination.

### REQ-16 Migration of existing permit records
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software offers comprehensive data migration services as part of the implementation process. Our team has previously migrated data from the City of Marlow Vale's current permit system on two separate occasions, giving us specific familiarity with the data structures and potential challenges involved. The migration process involves extracting data from database exports of the legacy system, cleansing and transforming it to fit the PermitFlow schema, and loading it into the new environment. We manage this entire process, ensuring that historical permit records, applicant details, and associated documents are accurately transferred to PermitFlow, allowing for seamless continuity of service and historical reference.

### REQ-17 Standard and custom reporting
**Compliance: Full**

PermitFlow includes a powerful reporting engine designed to meet the analytical needs of the Planning Department. Out of the box, the system provides 30 standard reports covering key metrics such as permit volumes, approval rates, inspection status, and fee collection. Additionally, the system features a user-friendly, drag-and-drop report builder that allows city staff to create custom reports without technical assistance. These reports can be scheduled and automatically emailed to stakeholders at defined intervals, ensuring that the city maintains up-to-date visibility into its permit operations.

### REQ-18 Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software provides technical support to the City of Marlow Vale during standard business hours (08:00–18:00 on working days) via phone and email. For critical incidents defined as severity-1 (complete outage of the platform), we offer a 24/7 on-call support line. This dedicated line ensures that any total service disruption is addressed immediately, regardless of the time of day. We target a 30-minute response time for these severity-1 incidents, ensuring that the city's critical services are restored with minimal delay. Non-critical issues are handled within the standard business hours support framework.

### REQ-19 On-premises deployment option
**Compliance: Not met**

PermitFlow is provided exclusively as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. There is no on-premises version of the software available for deployment within the City of Marlow Vale's own data center. 

*Explanation:* Our business model is focused on cloud delivery to ensure that all customers benefit from the latest security patches, feature updates, and high-availability infrastructure without the burden of managing servers. The cloud hosting model described in REQ-01 ensures data residency within the country, mitigating many of the concerns often associated with off-shore cloud solutions. If the city has a strict requirement for on-premises hosting, PermitFlow may not be a viable option. However, for authorities seeking a modern, low-maintenance, and secure solution, the SaaS model offers significant advantages in total cost of ownership and agility.

### REQ-20 Training for staff
**Compliance: Full**

Tessellate Civic Software includes comprehensive training services in the implementation plan. We deliver train-the-trainer sessions designed to empower the city's internal leads to become proficient in PermitFlow and subsequently train other staff members. Additionally, we provide a library of online video tutorials covering all major user roles and functions, including administrator configuration, planner workflows, inspector app usage, and public portal guidance. This blended approach ensures that the City of Marlow Vale staff receives initial deep-dive training while having ongoing access to self-paced learning resources to support new hires or refresh skills.

parts.title: 6. Implementation Plan
parts.body:
## 6. Implementation Plan

Our implementation plan is designed to deliver PermitFlow to the City of Marlow Vale within a strict 16-week timeline. As PermitFlow is a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform, our approach focuses on configuration, integration, data migration, and user adoption, rather than hardware installation or software deployment on local servers. We have successfully implemented PermitFlow for 41 other local authorities, and our methodology is standardized yet flexible enough to accommodate the City’s specific workflows.

The project is divided into five distinct phases. Below is the detailed breakdown of each phase, including the specific responsibilities of the City and Tessellate.

### Phase 1: Project Initiation and Setup (Weeks 1–2)

**Objective:** Establish the project foundation, define governance, and configure the core SaaS environment.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Project Kick-off:** Conduct a joint kick-off meeting with the City’s Project Manager, IT Security Officer, and Planning Department leads to finalize the project charter, communication plan, and escalation procedures.
*   **Environment Provisioning:** Provision the PermitFlow tenant in our secure, in-country data centers. This includes setting up the primary and failover environments.
*   **Core Configuration:** Configure basic system settings, including time zones, languages, currency (EUR), and email notification templates.
*   **Role Definition:** Set up the 12 predefined roles within the system and map them to the City’s existing job titles (e.g., Planning Officer, Inspector, Admin).

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Project Team Designation:** Appoint a dedicated Project Manager and a Technical Lead from the IT department to serve as primary points of contact.
*   **Stakeholder Identification:** Identify key users from the Planning Department who will provide input on workflows and testing.
*   **Infrastructure Access:** Provide necessary access details for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration, including SAML 2.0 metadata or OpenID Connect configuration files from the City’s Identity Provider (IdP).
*   **Approval of Configuration:** Review and approve the initial system configuration and role mappings.

### Phase 2: Data Migration and Integration (Weeks 3–7)

**Objective:** Securely migrate existing permit records and integrate PermitFlow with the City’s payment provider and identity provider.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Data Mapping:** Analyze the data structure of the City’s current permit system. We will create a detailed data mapping document correlating fields from the legacy system to PermitFlow.
*   **Migration Script Development:** Develop and test data transformation scripts. Having migrated from this specific product twice before, we will leverage existing knowledge of its schema to expedite this process.
*   **Payment Integration:** Configure the standard integration with the City’s existing online payment provider to enable fee payments via the public portal.
*   **SSO Configuration:** Finalize and test the SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect integration with the City’s Identity Provider to ensure seamless login and role-based access.
*   **First Data Migration Cycle:** Execute the first full data migration into the staging environment.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Data Extraction:** Provide database exports of all existing permit applications, inspections, payments, and user accounts from the current system in agreed-upon formats (e.g., SQL dumps, CSVs).
*   **Data Cleansing:** Review and clean data where possible (e.g., merging duplicate user accounts, correcting invalid addresses) before the final migration.
*   **Payment Provider Coordination:** Facilitate introductions or provide API keys/credentials required for the payment gateway integration.
*   **SSO Testing:** Collaborate with the IT Security Officer to test SSO login flows for various user roles and verify that multi-factor authentication (MFA) triggers correctly for administrators.
*   **Migration Validation:** Verify the accuracy of the migrated data in the staging environment against source records.

### Phase 3: Workflow Configuration and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) (Weeks 8–12)

**Objective:** Configure specific permit workflows, train super-users, and conduct rigorous testing.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Workflow Configuration:** Configure the permit application, review, and inspection workflows based on the City’s current and desired processes. This includes setting up routing rules for reviewers and inspectors.
*   **Report Configuration:** Set up the 30 standard reports and configure any custom reports required by the Planning Department using the drag-and-drop report builder.
*   **Super-User Training:** Conduct "Train-the-Trainer" sessions for designated super-users from the Planning Department. These sessions will cover administrative functions, workflow management, and report generation.
*   **UAT Support:** Provide a dedicated support channel for the UAT team to log issues and receive rapid feedback.
*   **Issue Resolution:** Address any defects or configuration issues identified during UAT.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **UAT Team Formation:** Assemble a UAT team comprising representatives from Planning, IT, and Finance.
*   **Scenario Testing:** Execute test scripts for end-to-end processes, including:
    *   Submitting a new application via the public portal.
    *   Assigning reviews and inspections.
    *   Processing payments.
    *   Viewing and marking up PDF plans in the electronic review tool.
    *   Submitting inspection results via the mobile app (online).
*   **Feedback and Sign-off:** Document test results, approve or reject configurations, and provide formal sign-off on the configured system once UAT is complete.
*   **Content Creation:** Draft and finalize standard email notifications, help texts, and public-facing instructions for the applicant portal.

### Phase 4: End-User Training and Final Data Migration (Weeks 13–14)

**Objective:** Train all end-users and perform the final data migration for production readiness.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **End-User Training Materials:** Provide online video tutorials and quick-reference guides for all user roles (Planning Officers, Inspectors, Admins). These resources will be available within the PermitFlow help portal.
*   **Final Data Migration:** Execute the final data migration into the production environment. This will be a "delta" migration to capture any changes made in the legacy system during the UAT phase.
*   **Data Verification:** Perform automated and manual checks to ensure data integrity in the production environment.
*   **Security Final Checks:** Confirm that all security settings, including MFA enforcement and audit logging, are active and configured as agreed.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Schedule Training:** Coordinate with Tessellate to schedule and announce the online training sessions to all staff.
*   **Staff Participation:** Ensure all users attend their designated training sessions and review the provided video materials.
*   **Legacy System Freeze:** Coordinate with the IT department to minimize or freeze changes to the legacy permit system during the final data migration window to ensure data consistency.
*   **Production Readiness Review:** Conduct a final review of the production environment with Tessellate to confirm readiness for go-live.

### Phase 5: Go-Live and Hypercare (Weeks 15–16)

**Objective:** Transition to live operations and provide intensive support during the initial weeks.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   **Go-Live Execution:** Switch the public portal and staff login URLs to point to the production environment. Disable access to the legacy system if agreed.
*   **Hypercare Support:** Provide enhanced support during the first two weeks of live operation. This includes daily check-ins with the City’s Project Manager and prioritized resolution of any live issues.
*   **Audit Log Verification:** Confirm that audit logs are capturing all activities as required for the first week of operations.
*   **Performance Monitoring:** Monitor system availability and performance metrics to ensure the 99.9% SLA is being met.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   **Public Communication:** Notify the public, developers, and other stakeholders that the new permit system is live and provide instructions on how to access it.
*   **Internal Communication:** Remind staff of the new login procedures and support channels.
*   **Legacy System Decommissioning:** Initiate the decommissioning process for the old permit system, ensuring all historical data is archived as required by the City’s retention policy.
*   **Issue Logging:** Report any live issues to Tessellate’s support team via the agreed channels.

### Post-Go-Live Support

After the 16-week implementation period, the City will transition to standard support services as defined in the RFP response. This includes business-hours support for general inquiries and 24/7 coverage for critical incidents (complete outage). The 14 open accessibility issues on internal staff screens identified in the pre-sales audit will be scheduled for remediation within the first six months post-contract signature, with regular progress updates provided to the City’s IT Security Officer.

This phased approach ensures a structured, collaborative, and low-risk transition to PermitFlow, leveraging our previous experience with the City’s legacy data to minimize migration risks and ensure a successful launch.

parts.title: 7. Pricing
parts.body:
7. Pricing

Tessellate offers a transparent and predictable pricing model for the PermitFlow platform. As a Software-as-a-Service provider, our pricing consists of an annual subscription fee that covers the core platform, infrastructure, and ongoing support, alongside one-off professional services fees for the initial implementation, data migration, and user training.

The following table outlines the costs associated with the City of Marlow Vale’s request for proposals (MV-2026-114). All prices are quoted in Euros (EUR) and are exclusive of VAT. No discounts are applied.

| **Cost Item** | **Type** | **Amount** | **Description** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Recurring | **€96,000** | Covers annual hosting, support services, and platform updates. |
| **Implementation & Data Migration** | One-off | **€38,000** | Covers system configuration, integration setup, and migration of existing permit records. |
| **Training** | One-off | **€6,500** | Covers train-the-trainer sessions and online video resources for staff. |

### Total Cost of Ownership

**First-Year Total**
The total investment required for the first year of service is **€140,500**. This figure includes the first annual subscription (€96,000), the one-off implementation and data migration fees (€38,000), and the one-off training costs (€6,500).

**Five-Year Total Cost**
Over a five-year period, the total cost is **€524,500**. This is calculated as five years of annual subscriptions (5 × €96,000 = €480,000) plus the one-off implementation, migration, and training costs (€38,000 + €6,500 = €44,500). 

This pricing structure ensures that the City of Marlow Vale receives a fully managed, high-availability solution with predictable ongoing costs. The annual subscription model eliminates the need for the City to invest in additional hardware or software licensing for the platform, allowing the Planning Department to focus its resources on community development and permit processing rather than IT maintenance.
