## Safety Information

## Safety Information

Your safety is our priority. Please read these warnings carefully before using your Hearthline T2 thermostat.

- **Qualified Installation Required:** The receiver box connects to your home’s electrical system and gas/oil boiler controls. It must be installed by a qualified gas safe or electrical engineer. Do not attempt to wire the receiver box yourself.
- **No Direct Sunlight:** Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight or above a radiator. Heat and light can affect the temperature sensor’s accuracy and may damage the screen over time.
- **Do Not Open the Receiver Box:** The receiver box contains mains voltage components. It must only be opened by a qualified installer. Attempting to open it yourself could result in serious injury or electric shock.
- **Battery Safety:** When replacing batteries in the wall unit, use 2 AA alkaline batteries only. Do not mix old and new batteries, or different types (alkaline, standard, rechargeable). Dispose of used batteries responsibly.
- **Keep Dry:** Keep the wall unit and receiver box away from water and moisture. Do not splash water on the screen or touch the device with wet hands.
- **Choking Hazard:** The AA batteries used in the wall unit are small parts. Keep them out of reach of young children to prevent choking.
- **Interference:** Electronic devices such as routers, baby monitors, or cordless phones may interfere with the radio signal between the wall unit and the receiver. If you experience connectivity issues, try moving the devices apart.
- **Child Supervision:** This product is not a toy. It can be accessed by children aged 8 years and above. Clean and user maintenance shall not be made by children without supervision.

## Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Wall Unit Screen** | 3.5-inch touch screen with rotating ring |
| **Wall Unit Power** | 2 AA batteries (approx. 2-year life) or 24 V AC wiring |
| **Receiver Box Power** | Mains powered |
| **Wi-Fi Connectivity** | 2.4 GHz only |
| **Radio Range** | Up to 30 m indoors between wall unit and receiver |
| **Installation Requirement** | Receiver box installation must be done by a qualified installer |

## Getting Started

Welcome to your new Hearthline T2. This chapter helps you get your smart thermostat ready to use. We will pair the screen with the box near your boiler, connect to Wi-Fi, and set up your account.

### How to

1.  **Insert batteries or connect wiring.** The wall unit runs on two AA batteries or 24 V AC wiring. If using batteries, put them in the back slot. Make sure the contacts touch. If wired, check with your installer that the 24 V supply is active.
2.  **Power on the wall unit.** Press and hold the center of the ring for three seconds. The screen will light up.
3.  **Pair the wall unit with the receiver.** The receiver box is the unit wired next to your boiler. It is already installed by your professional installer. On the wall unit screen, follow the on-screen prompt to pair. The units talk to each other by radio. This range is up to 30 meters indoors. Ensure no large metal objects block the signal.
4.  **Connect to Wi-Fi.** Select **Menu > Settings > Wi-Fi**. Your home Wi-Fi must be 2.4 GHz. If your router uses 5 GHz, you may need to connect to the 2.4 GHz band instead. Enter your Wi-Fi password using the on-screen keyboard.
5.  **Create your account.** Download the Hearthline app on iOS or Android. Open the app and follow the steps to create an account. You will link your thermostat to this account using the code shown on the wall unit screen.
6.  **Adjust basic preferences.** In the app or on the screen, set your language, temperature unit, and time format. See the Settings table below for details.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The wall unit screen is blank.** Check if the batteries are fresh and inserted correctly. If wired, check the fuse or transformer with your installer.
*   **Wi-Fi connection fails.** Ensure your router broadcasts a 2.4 GHz signal. The T2 does not support 5 GHz Wi-Fi. Move the receiver box or router closer to reduce interference.
*   **Pairing times out.** Move the wall unit closer to the receiver box temporarily. Ensure the receiver box is powered on. Try pairing again.

## Manual Temperature Control

You can change the temperature right from the wall unit or your phone. This is useful when you want a different temperature than your schedule provides.

### How to

1.  **Use the wall unit.** Rotate the ring clockwise to increase the temperature. Rotate it counter-clockwise to decrease it. The screen shows the target temperature in large numbers. Press the center of the ring to confirm your choice.
2.  **Use the app.** Open the Hearthline app. Tap on the current temperature display. A slider will appear. Drag the slider to set your desired temperature. Tap "Set" to save.
3.  **Set a hold.** If you want to keep the new temperature for a while, select **Menu > Heating > Hold** on the wall unit, or use the hold option in the app. Choose how long you want this temperature to last.
4.  **Return to schedule.** If you set a hold for a limited time, the thermostat returns to your schedule automatically. To cancel a hold immediately, go to **Menu > Heating > Hold** and select "End Hold".

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Target temperature | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps | 20 °C |
| Hold duration | Until next schedule change, 1–12 hours, or permanent | Until next schedule change |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature does not change.** Ensure the receiver box is responding. If the screen shows Error E3, check the receiver box power and location.
*   **The ring feels stuck.** Check if Child Lock is enabled. If the lock icon is on the screen, disable it in **Menu > Settings > Child Lock**.
*   **Changes in the app do not update the wall unit.** Check your Wi-Fi connection. Tap the refresh icon in the app to sync the status.

## Weekly Schedule

Your schedule tells the thermostat when to heat your home. By default, it follows a pattern that heats up in the morning, lowers during the day, and warms up in the evening.

### How to

1.  **Open the schedule editor.** On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. You can also edit the schedule in the Hearthline app.
2.  **Select a day.** Choose the day you want to edit, such as Monday or Saturday. You can copy a schedule from one day to another using the "Copy day" feature.
3.  **Edit the periods.** Each day is divided into periods. You can have 1 to 6 periods per day. Select a period to change the start time and temperature.
4.  **Add or remove periods.** If you need more control, add a period. If you need a simpler schedule, remove a period. The thermostat will automatically use the previous period's setting until the next one starts.
5.  **Save your schedule.** Confirm the changes. The thermostat will now follow your new plan. It will switch between settings at the exact times you chose.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Periods per day | 1–6 | 4 |
| Copy day | Any other days | N/A |
| Default periods | 06:30 20 °C, 08:30 17 °C, 17:00 21 °C, 22:30 16 °C | N/A |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature does not change at the scheduled time.** Check if a "Hold" is active. A hold overrides the schedule. End the hold to resume automatic control.
*   **Periods overlap.** If you see an error or unexpected behavior, ensure the start time of each period is later than the end time of the previous one. The system will not allow invalid time sequences.
*   **Schedule seems wrong after power loss.** The schedule is saved internally. If it resets to defaults, check if a factory reset was accidentally performed.

## 4. Away Mode and Geofencing

Away Mode helps you save energy when nobody is home. Instead of waiting for the heating schedule to change, the thermostat uses your phone's location. This is called "geofencing." A geofence is a virtual boundary around your home. When every household member's phone leaves this boundary, the thermostat drops the temperature to the Eco Temperature. When someone returns, the heating starts again.

### How to

1.  Open the Hearthline app.
2.  Tap **Menu > Heating > Away Mode**.
3.  Toggle **Geofencing** to **On**.
4.  Follow the prompts to grant location access on your phone.
5.  Invite other household members to join the home network so their phones also trigger Away Mode.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Geofence radius | 200–2,000 m | 500 m |
| Return pre-heat | On / Off | On |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Heating turns off when someone is still at home:** Check that the person's phone has location services enabled for the Hearthline app. Ensure they are connected to the same home network in the app.
*   **Heating does not turn on when returning home:** Ensure **Return pre-heat** is set to **On**. If it is Off, the heating only starts after the phone re-enters the geofence, which may cause a delay. Check your phone's battery saver mode, as it can block location updates.
*   **Geofence seems too large or too small:** Adjust the **Geofence radius** in **Menu > Heating > Away Mode**. A smaller radius (e.g., 200 m) prevents heating from starting if you are just driving past. A larger radius (e.g., 2,000 m) ensures heating is ready for larger properties or rural areas with poor GPS accuracy.

## 5. Eco Temperature

The Eco Temperature is the target temperature used during Away Mode and Frost Protection. It keeps your home comfortable enough to save energy without letting it get too cold. Setting this value correctly ensures your home doesn't feel chilly when you return.

### How to

1.  Tap the **Menu** button on the wall unit or open the app.
2.  Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature**.
3.  Turn the ring or use the app arrows to set your desired temperature.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Eco temperature | 10–20 °C | 16 °C |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Home feels too cold during Away Mode:** Increase the **Eco temperature** by 1 or 2 °C. Note that this may slightly increase energy usage.
*   **Eco Temperature change doesn't take effect:** Wait until the next scheduled period or Away Mode trigger. The Eco Temperature is primarily applied when Away Mode is active or when the schedule dictates an eco period. It does not change your standard heating schedule targets.

## 6. Boost

Boost is a quick way to make your home warmer right now. You might use it if you have a guest arriving unexpectedly or if it has suddenly turned cold outside. When Boost is active, the thermostat raises the target temperature above your usual setting for a short time.

### How to

1.  Tap the **Menu** button on the wall unit.
2.  Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost**.
3.  Select the **Boost duration**.
4.  Confirm the selection by pressing the ring or tapping **Start** in the app.
5.  To cancel early, select **Cancel Boost**.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Boost duration | 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes | 60 minutes |
| Boost temperature | Default target + 2 °C | Default target + 2 °C |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Home does not warm up:** Check that your boiler is running. Look for the flame icon on the wall unit. If there is no flame, check your boiler power or error codes.
*   **Temperature does not rise by 2 °C:** The Boost temperature is always 2 °C higher than your *current* target temperature. If you manually lower the target temperature while Boost is active, the Boost target lowers too. Ensure your manual target is set to your usual comfort level before starting Boost.
*   **Boost ends too quickly:** You may have selected **30 minutes**. Select a longer duration next time. You can also restart Boost if you need more heat.

## 7. Hot Water Control

The Hearthline T2 manages your hot water supply if your home has a hot water cylinder (also called a tank). This feature ensures you have hot water when you need it, without keeping the boiler running all day. If your home does not have a hot water cylinder, you can ignore this chapter.

### How to

1. **Enable Hot Water Control**: 
   - Go to the app and select **Menu > Heating > Hot Water**.
   - Toggle **Hot Water Control** to **On**.
   - Select the type of heating system you have when prompted.

2. **Set a Hot Water Schedule**:
   - In the app, go to **Menu > Heating > Hot Water > Schedule**.
   - Choose the day you want to edit.
   - Tap **Add Period**. You can add up to 3 periods per day.
   - Set the **Start Time** and **End Time** for each period.
   - During these times, the boiler will heat the water in the cylinder.

3. **Use Hot Water Boost**:
   - If you need extra hot water right now, open the app.
   - Tap **Boost** on the main screen, then select **Hot Water**.
   - Choose **30 minutes** or **60 minutes**.
   - The boiler will start heating the water immediately, overriding the current schedule for that duration.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hot Water Schedule | Up to 3 periods per day | None |
| Hot Water Boost | 30 or 60 minutes | 60 minutes |

### Troubleshooting

- **No hot water is being produced**: Check that **Hot Water Control** is turned **On** in the app. Verify that the current time is within one of your scheduled periods.
- **The hot water boost doesn't start**: Ensure your wall unit is paired correctly with the receiver box. If you are using the app, check that you are connected to Wi-Fi. If you are at the wall unit, check that the batteries have sufficient charge.
- **The boiler runs when not scheduled**: This may happen if you have recently used **Hot Water Boost**. Wait for the boost duration (30 or 60 minutes) to finish. If the issue persists, check your schedule to ensure no periods are accidentally enabled.

## 8. Holiday Mode

Holiday Mode is perfect for when you are away from home for several days or weeks. It maintains a low, safe temperature to protect your home from freezing while saving energy compared to full heating. You do not need to use Away Mode or Geofencing during Holiday Mode.

### How to

1. **Start Holiday Mode**:
   - Open the Hearthline app.
   - Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday Mode**.
   - Select **Start Date** and **End Date**.
   - Confirm the settings.
   - Alternatively, at the wall unit, turn the ring to select **Holiday Mode** and press the center button.

2. **Check Status**:
   - While Holiday Mode is active, the screen on the wall unit will display a snowflake icon or the text "Holiday".
   - In the app, the main screen will show a **Holiday Mode** banner.

3. **End Holiday Mode Early**:
   - Open the app and go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday Mode**.
   - Tap **Stop** to return to your normal weekly schedule immediately.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Start and End Dates | Calendar dates | None |
| Holiday Temperature | 5–15 °C | 12 °C |

### Troubleshooting

- **Holiday Mode does not start**: Ensure the date and time on the wall unit or app are correct. Check that your phone is connected to Wi-Fi if starting via the app.

- **The temperature seems too low**: Holiday Mode sets the room temperature to a low level to save energy. This is normal. If you feel cold when you return early, you can exit Holiday Mode via the app or wall unit to resume your normal schedule.

- **The date is wrong**: Check the time zone settings in the app under **Profile > Home Settings**. The system uses your home’s time zone for schedules.

## 9. Frost Protection

Frost Protection is a critical safety feature. It automatically turns on your heating if the room temperature drops below a safe level, even if your schedule says the heating should be off. This prevents your pipes from bursting in cold weather.

**Important:** Frost Protection **cannot** be turned off. It is always active to ensure your home’s safety.

### How to

1. **Check Frost Protection Status**:
   - Frost Protection works automatically. You do not need to switch it on.
   - To see if it is active, look at the app’s main screen. If the temperature is very low, the app may show "Frost Protection Active".

2. **Adjust the Frost Temperature**:
   - You can change the temperature at which the heating kicks in.
   - Go to **Menu > Heating > Frost Protection** in the app.
   - Use the slider to set your preferred **Frost Temperature**.
   - Press **Save**.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frost Temperature | 5–12 °C | 7 °C |

### Troubleshooting

- **The heating turns on when it shouldn’t**: Check the current room temperature. If it is below the **Frost Temperature** (default 7 °C), the system will heat to prevent freezing. This is normal behavior.

- **I want to disable Frost Protection**: You cannot disable this feature. It is a mandatory safety requirement for the Hearthline T2. If you wish to have no heating at all, consider turning off your boiler at the mains, but be aware that this leaves your property vulnerable to damage in very cold weather.

- **The temperature reading is inaccurate**: Ensure the wall unit is not installed in direct sunlight or above a radiator, as heat sources can affect the sensor. If the issue continues, check for error code **E2** (Temperature Sensor Fault) and contact support if necessary.

### Chapter 10: Energy Reports

Want to see how much energy your heating uses? Energy Reports help you understand your habits. You can spot leaks, track boiler usage, and save money. Reports are stored in the Hearthline app. You can also get a weekly summary by email.

#### How to

1.  Open the Hearthline app on your smartphone.
2.  Tap the **Energy** tab at the bottom of the screen.
3.  Choose **Weekly Email** to turn email reports on or off. 
4.  Tap **Monthly Summary** to view a longer trend. This summary is always created automatically.
5.  Look at **Boiler Running Hours** to see how many hours your boiler ran each day. This helps you see if your heating is working too hard.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Weekly email | On or Off | On |
| Monthly summary in the app | Always on | On |
| Boiler running hours shown per day | Displayed automatically | On |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **No weekly email arrives.** Check your spam or junk folder. Ensure your email address in the app is correct. Tap **Resend** if available in the app settings.
*   **Boiler running hours seem wrong.** The system calculates hours based on when the boiler is actively heating. It does not count hot water time unless it triggers heating. Check if your schedule is set correctly.
*   **Energy tab is empty.** Wait 24 hours after installation. Data needs time to collect. Ensure your Wi-Fi is connected, as the app pulls data from the cloud.

### Chapter 11: Child Lock

Do you have young children? The Child Lock stops them from changing the temperature or schedule. When Child Lock is on, the ring and screen on the wall unit do not react to touches. You can still change settings in the app.

#### How to

1.  Press the ring on the wall unit once to wake the screen.
2.  Hold the ring for five seconds. You will see a lock symbol appear.
3.  The first time you turn on Child Lock, you must create a PIN. Use four digits.
4.  Enter the PIN again to confirm it.
5.  To turn Child Lock off, press the ring and enter the PIN. 

If you are in the app, go to **Settings > Device > Child Lock** to toggle it on or off. You must have the PIN to change this setting in the app as well.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Lock | On or Off | Off |
| PIN | 4 digits | Set when lock is first turned on |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **I forgot my PIN.** You must reset the wall unit to factory settings to clear the PIN. This will remove your schedule. Go to **Settings > System > Reset** in the app if the wall unit is locked, or hold the pairing button on the receiver for 10 seconds to reset both devices. You will need to pair them again.
*   **The screen is locked but I want to change the temp.** Use the Hearthline app. Child Lock only blocks the physical wall unit. The app is not affected by the lock on the wall unit.
*   **The lock symbol is on but touches work.** Check if you accidentally turned Child Lock off in the app. Try locking it again from the wall unit by holding the ring for five seconds.

### Chapter 12: Multi-User Access

Everyone in your home can use the thermostat. You can invite up to eight people. Each person gets their own login. You can choose what each person is allowed to do.

#### Roles

It is important to understand the three roles:

*   **Owner:** This is the first person who creates the account. The Owner can invite people, remove people, and change everything. There is only one Owner.
*   **Member:** A Member can change the temperature and the schedule. They can turn on Boost or Away Mode. They cannot invite new users or delete devices.
*   **Guest:** A Guest can only change the current temperature. They **cannot** change the schedule. This is good for visitors or cleaners who should not mess up your heating plan.

#### How to

1.  Open the Hearthline app.
2.  Tap the **Profile** icon in the top right corner.
3.  Select **Manage Users**.
4.  Tap **Invite New User**.
5.  Enter the person’s email address.
6.  Choose their role: **Member** or **Guest**. The Owner role is fixed for the account creator.
7.  The person will get an email. They must download the Hearthline app and create an account to join.

To change someone’s role later, go to **Manage Users**, tap their name, and select **Change Role**.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Users | Up to 8 per home | 1 (Owner only) |
| Roles | Owner, Member, Guest | Owner |
| Guests change schedule | No (locked) | No |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **Invitation email does not arrive.** Ask the person to check their spam folder. Check if you typed the email address correctly. You can resend the invite from the **Manage Users** screen.
*   **A Member cannot change the schedule.** Check their role. If they are set as a Guest, they cannot change the schedule. Change their role to Member in the app.
*   **I reached the limit of 8 users.** Remove a user who no longer lives in the home. Tap **Manage Users**, select the name, and tap **Remove**. The slot will free up immediately.
*   **Guest can change temperature.** This is correct. Guests can change the current temperature. They just cannot save changes to the weekly schedule. Check if they are actually editing the schedule in the app. Ensure the app is updated to the latest version.

## Error Codes

# Error Codes

If your Hearthline T2 shows a code on the screen or app, don't worry. Here is what the codes mean and what you can do to fix the issue.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **E1** | No Wi-Fi connection | Check your router to ensure it is on. Ensure your phone is connected to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Restart the receiver box by unplugging it for 10 seconds. |
| **E2** | Temperature sensor fault | This indicates a fault with the internal temperature sensor. Turn off the power to the receiver box at the fuse box. Wait 1 minute. Turn it back on. If the error remains, contact support. |
| **E3** | Receiver not responding | The wall unit cannot see the receiver box. Move the wall unit closer to the receiver if possible. Check if the receiver box has power (the light should be on). Change the batteries in the wall unit. |
| **E4** | Wall unit battery low | Replace the two AA batteries in the wall unit with new alkaline batteries. Make sure they are inserted with the correct polarity (+/-). The code will clear automatically after a few minutes. |
| **E5** | Firmware update failed | Do not turn off the device. Open the Hearthline app and go to **Menu > System > Update**. Try the update again. Ensure the device stays connected to power or has fresh batteries during the process. |

If the error code persists after following these steps, please contact our customer support team for further assistance.

## Specifications

# Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Wall Unit Display** | 3.5-inch touch screen |
| **Wall Unit Power** | 2 AA batteries (approx. 2 years life) or 24 V AC wiring |
| **Receiver Box Power** | Mains powered |
| **Wi-Fi** | 2.4 GHz only |
| **Radio Range** | Up to 30 m indoors between receiver and wall unit |
| **Installation** | Receiver box installation must be done by a qualified installer |

parts.title: Safety Information
parts.body:
## Safety Information

Your safety is our priority. Please read these warnings carefully before using your Hearthline T2 thermostat.

- **Qualified Installation Required:** The receiver box connects to your home’s electrical system and gas/oil boiler controls. It must be installed by a qualified gas safe or electrical engineer. Do not attempt to wire the receiver box yourself.
- **No Direct Sunlight:** Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight or above a radiator. Heat and light can affect the temperature sensor’s accuracy and may damage the screen over time.
- **Do Not Open the Receiver Box:** The receiver box contains mains voltage components. It must only be opened by a qualified installer. Attempting to open it yourself could result in serious injury or electric shock.
- **Battery Safety:** When replacing batteries in the wall unit, use 2 AA alkaline batteries only. Do not mix old and new batteries, or different types (alkaline, standard, rechargeable). Dispose of used batteries responsibly.
- **Keep Dry:** Keep the wall unit and receiver box away from water and moisture. Do not splash water on the screen or touch the device with wet hands.
- **Choking Hazard:** The AA batteries used in the wall unit are small parts. Keep them out of reach of young children to prevent choking.
- **Interference:** Electronic devices such as routers, baby monitors, or cordless phones may interfere with the radio signal between the wall unit and the receiver. If you experience connectivity issues, try moving the devices apart.
- **Child Supervision:** This product is not a toy. It can be accessed by children aged 8 years and above. Clean and user maintenance shall not be made by children without supervision.

## Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Wall Unit Screen** | 3.5-inch touch screen with rotating ring |
| **Wall Unit Power** | 2 AA batteries (approx. 2-year life) or 24 V AC wiring |
| **Receiver Box Power** | Mains powered |
| **Wi-Fi Connectivity** | 2.4 GHz only |
| **Radio Range** | Up to 30 m indoors between wall unit and receiver |
| **Installation Requirement** | Receiver box installation must be done by a qualified installer |

## Getting Started

Welcome to your new Hearthline T2. This chapter helps you get your smart thermostat ready to use. We will pair the screen with the box near your boiler, connect to Wi-Fi, and set up your account.

### How to

1.  **Insert batteries or connect wiring.** The wall unit runs on two AA batteries or 24 V AC wiring. If using batteries, put them in the back slot. Make sure the contacts touch. If wired, check with your installer that the 24 V supply is active.
2.  **Power on the wall unit.** Press and hold the center of the ring for three seconds. The screen will light up.
3.  **Pair the wall unit with the receiver.** The receiver box is the unit wired next to your boiler. It is already installed by your professional installer. On the wall unit screen, follow the on-screen prompt to pair. The units talk to each other by radio. This range is up to 30 meters indoors. Ensure no large metal objects block the signal.
4.  **Connect to Wi-Fi.** Select **Menu > Settings > Wi-Fi**. Your home Wi-Fi must be 2.4 GHz. If your router uses 5 GHz, you may need to connect to the 2.4 GHz band instead. Enter your Wi-Fi password using the on-screen keyboard.
5.  **Create your account.** Download the Hearthline app on iOS or Android. Open the app and follow the steps to create an account. You will link your thermostat to this account using the code shown on the wall unit screen.
6.  **Adjust basic preferences.** In the app or on the screen, set your language, temperature unit, and time format. See the Settings table below for details.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The wall unit screen is blank.** Check if the batteries are fresh and inserted correctly. If wired, check the fuse or transformer with your installer.
*   **Wi-Fi connection fails.** Ensure your router broadcasts a 2.4 GHz signal. The T2 does not support 5 GHz Wi-Fi. Move the receiver box or router closer to reduce interference.
*   **Pairing times out.** Move the wall unit closer to the receiver box temporarily. Ensure the receiver box is powered on. Try pairing again.

## Manual Temperature Control

You can change the temperature right from the wall unit or your phone. This is useful when you want a different temperature than your schedule provides.

### How to

1.  **Use the wall unit.** Rotate the ring clockwise to increase the temperature. Rotate it counter-clockwise to decrease it. The screen shows the target temperature in large numbers. Press the center of the ring to confirm your choice.
2.  **Use the app.** Open the Hearthline app. Tap on the current temperature display. A slider will appear. Drag the slider to set your desired temperature. Tap "Set" to save.
3.  **Set a hold.** If you want to keep the new temperature for a while, select **Menu > Heating > Hold** on the wall unit, or use the hold option in the app. Choose how long you want this temperature to last.
4.  **Return to schedule.** If you set a hold for a limited time, the thermostat returns to your schedule automatically. To cancel a hold immediately, go to **Menu > Heating > Hold** and select "End Hold".

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Target temperature | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps | 20 °C |
| Hold duration | Until next schedule change, 1–12 hours, or permanent | Until next schedule change |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature does not change.** Ensure the receiver box is responding. If the screen shows Error E3, check the receiver box power and location.
*   **The ring feels stuck.** Check if Child Lock is enabled. If the lock icon is on the screen, disable it in **Menu > Settings > Child Lock**.
*   **Changes in the app do not update the wall unit.** Check your Wi-Fi connection. Tap the refresh icon in the app to sync the status.

## Weekly Schedule

Your schedule tells the thermostat when to heat your home. By default, it follows a pattern that heats up in the morning, lowers during the day, and warms up in the evening.

### How to

1.  **Open the schedule editor.** On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. You can also edit the schedule in the Hearthline app.
2.  **Select a day.** Choose the day you want to edit, such as Monday or Saturday. You can copy a schedule from one day to another using the "Copy day" feature.
3.  **Edit the periods.** Each day is divided into periods. You can have 1 to 6 periods per day. Select a period to change the start time and temperature.
4.  **Add or remove periods.** If you need more control, add a period. If you need a simpler schedule, remove a period. The thermostat will automatically use the previous period's setting until the next one starts.
5.  **Save your schedule.** Confirm the changes. The thermostat will now follow your new plan. It will switch between settings at the exact times you chose.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Periods per day | 1–6 | 4 |
| Copy day | Any other days | N/A |
| Default periods | 06:30 20 °C, 08:30 17 °C, 17:00 21 °C, 22:30 16 °C | N/A |

### Troubleshooting

*   **The temperature does not change at the scheduled time.** Check if a "Hold" is active. A hold overrides the schedule. End the hold to resume automatic control.
*   **Periods overlap.** If you see an error or unexpected behavior, ensure the start time of each period is later than the end time of the previous one. The system will not allow invalid time sequences.
*   **Schedule seems wrong after power loss.** The schedule is saved internally. If it resets to defaults, check if a factory reset was accidentally performed.

## 4. Away Mode and Geofencing

Away Mode helps you save energy when nobody is home. Instead of waiting for the heating schedule to change, the thermostat uses your phone's location. This is called "geofencing." A geofence is a virtual boundary around your home. When every household member's phone leaves this boundary, the thermostat drops the temperature to the Eco Temperature. When someone returns, the heating starts again.

### How to

1.  Open the Hearthline app.
2.  Tap **Menu > Heating > Away Mode**.
3.  Toggle **Geofencing** to **On**.
4.  Follow the prompts to grant location access on your phone.
5.  Invite other household members to join the home network so their phones also trigger Away Mode.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Geofence radius | 200–2,000 m | 500 m |
| Return pre-heat | On / Off | On |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Heating turns off when someone is still at home:** Check that the person's phone has location services enabled for the Hearthline app. Ensure they are connected to the same home network in the app.
*   **Heating does not turn on when returning home:** Ensure **Return pre-heat** is set to **On**. If it is Off, the heating only starts after the phone re-enters the geofence, which may cause a delay. Check your phone's battery saver mode, as it can block location updates.
*   **Geofence seems too large or too small:** Adjust the **Geofence radius** in **Menu > Heating > Away Mode**. A smaller radius (e.g., 200 m) prevents heating from starting if you are just driving past. A larger radius (e.g., 2,000 m) ensures heating is ready for larger properties or rural areas with poor GPS accuracy.

## 5. Eco Temperature

The Eco Temperature is the target temperature used during Away Mode and Frost Protection. It keeps your home comfortable enough to save energy without letting it get too cold. Setting this value correctly ensures your home doesn't feel chilly when you return.

### How to

1.  Tap the **Menu** button on the wall unit or open the app.
2.  Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature**.
3.  Turn the ring or use the app arrows to set your desired temperature.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Eco temperature | 10–20 °C | 16 °C |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Home feels too cold during Away Mode:** Increase the **Eco temperature** by 1 or 2 °C. Note that this may slightly increase energy usage.
*   **Eco Temperature change doesn't take effect:** Wait until the next scheduled period or Away Mode trigger. The Eco Temperature is primarily applied when Away Mode is active or when the schedule dictates an eco period. It does not change your standard heating schedule targets.

## 6. Boost

Boost is a quick way to make your home warmer right now. You might use it if you have a guest arriving unexpectedly or if it has suddenly turned cold outside. When Boost is active, the thermostat raises the target temperature above your usual setting for a short time.

### How to

1.  Tap the **Menu** button on the wall unit.
2.  Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost**.
3.  Select the **Boost duration**.
4.  Confirm the selection by pressing the ring or tapping **Start** in the app.
5.  To cancel early, select **Cancel Boost**.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Boost duration | 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes | 60 minutes |
| Boost temperature | Default target + 2 °C | Default target + 2 °C |

### Troubleshooting

*   **Home does not warm up:** Check that your boiler is running. Look for the flame icon on the wall unit. If there is no flame, check your boiler power or error codes.
*   **Temperature does not rise by 2 °C:** The Boost temperature is always 2 °C higher than your *current* target temperature. If you manually lower the target temperature while Boost is active, the Boost target lowers too. Ensure your manual target is set to your usual comfort level before starting Boost.
*   **Boost ends too quickly:** You may have selected **30 minutes**. Select a longer duration next time. You can also restart Boost if you need more heat.

## 7. Hot Water Control

The Hearthline T2 manages your hot water supply if your home has a hot water cylinder (also called a tank). This feature ensures you have hot water when you need it, without keeping the boiler running all day. If your home does not have a hot water cylinder, you can ignore this chapter.

### How to

1. **Enable Hot Water Control**: 
   - Go to the app and select **Menu > Heating > Hot Water**.
   - Toggle **Hot Water Control** to **On**.
   - Select the type of heating system you have when prompted.

2. **Set a Hot Water Schedule**:
   - In the app, go to **Menu > Heating > Hot Water > Schedule**.
   - Choose the day you want to edit.
   - Tap **Add Period**. You can add up to 3 periods per day.
   - Set the **Start Time** and **End Time** for each period.
   - During these times, the boiler will heat the water in the cylinder.

3. **Use Hot Water Boost**:
   - If you need extra hot water right now, open the app.
   - Tap **Boost** on the main screen, then select **Hot Water**.
   - Choose **30 minutes** or **60 minutes**.
   - The boiler will start heating the water immediately, overriding the current schedule for that duration.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hot Water Schedule | Up to 3 periods per day | None |
| Hot Water Boost | 30 or 60 minutes | 60 minutes |

### Troubleshooting

- **No hot water is being produced**: Check that **Hot Water Control** is turned **On** in the app. Verify that the current time is within one of your scheduled periods.
- **The hot water boost doesn't start**: Ensure your wall unit is paired correctly with the receiver box. If you are using the app, check that you are connected to Wi-Fi. If you are at the wall unit, check that the batteries have sufficient charge.
- **The boiler runs when not scheduled**: This may happen if you have recently used **Hot Water Boost**. Wait for the boost duration (30 or 60 minutes) to finish. If the issue persists, check your schedule to ensure no periods are accidentally enabled.

## 8. Holiday Mode

Holiday Mode is perfect for when you are away from home for several days or weeks. It maintains a low, safe temperature to protect your home from freezing while saving energy compared to full heating. You do not need to use Away Mode or Geofencing during Holiday Mode.

### How to

1. **Start Holiday Mode**:
   - Open the Hearthline app.
   - Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday Mode**.
   - Select **Start Date** and **End Date**.
   - Confirm the settings.
   - Alternatively, at the wall unit, turn the ring to select **Holiday Mode** and press the center button.

2. **Check Status**:
   - While Holiday Mode is active, the screen on the wall unit will display a snowflake icon or the text "Holiday".
   - In the app, the main screen will show a **Holiday Mode** banner.

3. **End Holiday Mode Early**:
   - Open the app and go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday Mode**.
   - Tap **Stop** to return to your normal weekly schedule immediately.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Start and End Dates | Calendar dates | None |
| Holiday Temperature | 5–15 °C | 12 °C |

### Troubleshooting

- **Holiday Mode does not start**: Ensure the date and time on the wall unit or app are correct. Check that your phone is connected to Wi-Fi if starting via the app.

- **The temperature seems too low**: Holiday Mode sets the room temperature to a low level to save energy. This is normal. If you feel cold when you return early, you can exit Holiday Mode via the app or wall unit to resume your normal schedule.

- **The date is wrong**: Check the time zone settings in the app under **Profile > Home Settings**. The system uses your home’s time zone for schedules.

## 9. Frost Protection

Frost Protection is a critical safety feature. It automatically turns on your heating if the room temperature drops below a safe level, even if your schedule says the heating should be off. This prevents your pipes from bursting in cold weather.

**Important:** Frost Protection **cannot** be turned off. It is always active to ensure your home’s safety.

### How to

1. **Check Frost Protection Status**:
   - Frost Protection works automatically. You do not need to switch it on.
   - To see if it is active, look at the app’s main screen. If the temperature is very low, the app may show "Frost Protection Active".

2. **Adjust the Frost Temperature**:
   - You can change the temperature at which the heating kicks in.
   - Go to **Menu > Heating > Frost Protection** in the app.
   - Use the slider to set your preferred **Frost Temperature**.
   - Press **Save**.

### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frost Temperature | 5–12 °C | 7 °C |

### Troubleshooting

- **The heating turns on when it shouldn’t**: Check the current room temperature. If it is below the **Frost Temperature** (default 7 °C), the system will heat to prevent freezing. This is normal behavior.

- **I want to disable Frost Protection**: You cannot disable this feature. It is a mandatory safety requirement for the Hearthline T2. If you wish to have no heating at all, consider turning off your boiler at the mains, but be aware that this leaves your property vulnerable to damage in very cold weather.

- **The temperature reading is inaccurate**: Ensure the wall unit is not installed in direct sunlight or above a radiator, as heat sources can affect the sensor. If the issue continues, check for error code **E2** (Temperature Sensor Fault) and contact support if necessary.

### Chapter 10: Energy Reports

Want to see how much energy your heating uses? Energy Reports help you understand your habits. You can spot leaks, track boiler usage, and save money. Reports are stored in the Hearthline app. You can also get a weekly summary by email.

#### How to

1.  Open the Hearthline app on your smartphone.
2.  Tap the **Energy** tab at the bottom of the screen.
3.  Choose **Weekly Email** to turn email reports on or off. 
4.  Tap **Monthly Summary** to view a longer trend. This summary is always created automatically.
5.  Look at **Boiler Running Hours** to see how many hours your boiler ran each day. This helps you see if your heating is working too hard.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Weekly email | On or Off | On |
| Monthly summary in the app | Always on | On |
| Boiler running hours shown per day | Displayed automatically | On |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **No weekly email arrives.** Check your spam or junk folder. Ensure your email address in the app is correct. Tap **Resend** if available in the app settings.
*   **Boiler running hours seem wrong.** The system calculates hours based on when the boiler is actively heating. It does not count hot water time unless it triggers heating. Check if your schedule is set correctly.
*   **Energy tab is empty.** Wait 24 hours after installation. Data needs time to collect. Ensure your Wi-Fi is connected, as the app pulls data from the cloud.

### Chapter 11: Child Lock

Do you have young children? The Child Lock stops them from changing the temperature or schedule. When Child Lock is on, the ring and screen on the wall unit do not react to touches. You can still change settings in the app.

#### How to

1.  Press the ring on the wall unit once to wake the screen.
2.  Hold the ring for five seconds. You will see a lock symbol appear.
3.  The first time you turn on Child Lock, you must create a PIN. Use four digits.
4.  Enter the PIN again to confirm it.
5.  To turn Child Lock off, press the ring and enter the PIN. 

If you are in the app, go to **Settings > Device > Child Lock** to toggle it on or off. You must have the PIN to change this setting in the app as well.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Lock | On or Off | Off |
| PIN | 4 digits | Set when lock is first turned on |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **I forgot my PIN.** You must reset the wall unit to factory settings to clear the PIN. This will remove your schedule. Go to **Settings > System > Reset** in the app if the wall unit is locked, or hold the pairing button on the receiver for 10 seconds to reset both devices. You will need to pair them again.
*   **The screen is locked but I want to change the temp.** Use the Hearthline app. Child Lock only blocks the physical wall unit. The app is not affected by the lock on the wall unit.
*   **The lock symbol is on but touches work.** Check if you accidentally turned Child Lock off in the app. Try locking it again from the wall unit by holding the ring for five seconds.

### Chapter 12: Multi-User Access

4.  Tap **Invite New User**.
5.  Enter the person’s email address.
6.  Choose their role: **Member** or **Guest**. The Owner role is fixed for the account creator.
7.  The person will get an email. They must download the Hearthline app and create an account to join.

To change someone’s role later, go to **Manage Users**, tap their name, and select **Change Role**.

#### Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Users | Up to 8 per home | 1 (Owner only) |
| Roles | Owner, Member, Guest | Owner |
| Guests change schedule | No (locked) | No |

#### Troubleshooting

*   **Invitation email does not arrive.** Ask the person to check their spam folder. Check if you typed the email address correctly. You can resend the invite from the **Manage Users** screen.
*   **A Member cannot change the schedule.** Check their role. If they are set as a Guest, they cannot change the schedule. Change their role to Member in the app.

This is followed by intelligent automation capabilities in features-4-6, specifically "Away Mode" and "Geofencing," which use location data to switch to "Eco Temperature" when the home is empty and restore schedules upon return. The final feature section, features-10-12, introduces "Energy Reports," enabling users to monitor heating efficiency, track boiler usage, and identify leaks via the app’s "Energy" tab, with options for weekly email summaries.

Two new sections have been added to support maintenance and reference. The "Error Codes" section provides a diagnostic table to resolve common issues, such as E1 for lost Wi-Fi connections, recommending router checks, 2.4 GHz verification, and receiver box restarts. Finally, the "Specifications" section outlines key hardware metrics, including a 3.5-inch touch screen wall unit, 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi, a 30-meter indoor radio range, and the necessity of mains power for the receiver box. Collectively, the document now offers a complete user journey: it ensures safe deployment through mandatory professional installation guidelines, facilitates initial setup and network configuration, leverages location-based automation and specific hot water controls for energy optimization, provides data-driven insights through energy monitoring, and equips users with immediate troubleshooting steps for error codes and quick access to technical specifications. This holistic approach supports users from initial compliance and setup through sophisticated automation and long-term system management, ensuring they can safely deploy, optimize, and maintain the Hearthline T2 thermostat.
